To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a subset of variables, including nC18, the ratio of nC22/phytane and the amount of residual dry oil, is effective for distinguishing differences in residual oil amounts among treatments by multivariate statistical methods.

1) the amount of residual oil was best predicted from a subset of three variables: nC18, nC22 and the sum of the amounts of hydrocarboms nC18-n C27, 2) the amount of phytane, ratio of n C18 to phytane, amount of residual dry oil, and nC22 were most successful in discriminating differences among treatments, 3) the amount of oil that disappeared by natural causes was not different among

the subset of variables nC18, nC22 and phytane was effective in predicting residual oil and the subset of variables phytane, ratio of n C18/phytate and residual dry oil was effective for distinguishing differences in treatment methods by multivariate analysis and its associated canonical analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a methodology that can be used in a variety of situations to select an optimum set of hydrocarbon variables that will be effective for prediction of residual hydrocarbon amounts and for assessing differences in treatment effects.
the development of a statistical protocol for selection of variables to assess the effectiveness of nutrient enrichment methods for reducing residual oil amounts on contaminated beaches.
selection of a subset of hydrocarbon variables that can predict the amount of residual oil on a beach and can distinguish differences in treatment application methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

nC18 and phytane are good indicators of residual oil amounts on oiled beaches, but phytane, in combination with the other variables, is a better indicator for distinguishing differences between fertilization methods.
the subset of variables nC18, nC22/phytane and phytane were effective in distinguishing differences in residual oil amounts among the treatment methods.
the most effective variables for prediction of residual oil and for assessment of differences among treatments were phytane and the sum of hydrocarbons, nC18-n27.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the application methods of nitrogen and phosphorous fertilizers to oile beaches can significantly reduce residual oil amounts.

a combination of hydrocarbons and residual oil amount can be used for assessing bioremediation effectiveness on oiled beaches and that multivariate statistics can be used to identify the best subset of variables for this purpose.

the use of multivariate statistical procedures was effective for selection of an optimal subset of hydrocarbon variables for assessment of residual oil reduction and for determining significant differences in treatment application methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combination of hydrocarbon variables, selected for their ability to predict residual oil amounts and distinguish treatment differences, can be used to assess effectiveness of nutrient applications in reducing residual oil on nutrient-enriched beaches.

the use of multivariate statistical techniques can be a useful approach for selecting a subset of hydrocarbon variables that can be used to assess the effectiveness of bioremediating residual oil on nutrient-enriched beaches.
multivariate statistical analysis can be used to determine the optimum set of variables for predicting and assessing differences in residual oil on nutrient-enriched beaches.
